design\architecture\initial description\desktop app.md:17:  - WebSocket: when "remote control" is activated, the Electron app starts a WebSocket server that the React app can connect to.
design\architecture\initial description\desktop app.md:20:    - The same server also serves the bundled React build over plain http on GET (index at `/`, assets by path, path traversal rejected, no directory listing); the WebSocket upgrade shares the one port. A LAN browser opens the QR/link, loads the app from the server, reads the token from the URL fragment and connects same-origin (`ws://` derived from `window.location`) with no manual dialog. Traffic is unencrypted on the user's own LAN; the token still gates access, and non-secure-context browser API gaps (async clipboard, service workers) need fallbacks.
design\releases\0_0_3\F_73_drag_card_to_first_place_fails.md:27:- Apply the same relinking for same-column and cross-column moves; cross-column moves also update `status`.
design\releases\0_0_3\F_73_drag_card_to_first_place_fails.md:35:- Cross-column moves update status and preserve valid chains in both columns.
design\releases\0_1_0\B_99_mobile_status_change_no_update.md:16:When connected through a websocket, when the backend changes the state of a card, the react side is not notified. A reload is currently needed. Most likely a missing message
design\releases\0_1_0\B_99_mobile_status_change_no_update.md:20:Here, card state means `status` in card Markdown frontmatter. Electron's project watcher sends file changes as `watchProject` WebSocket events. Mobile client then requests changed file through `RemoteControlStorageService.loadFile`; `ProjectLoading` reparses it, and `DataService` should publish card-level and collection-level `status` events consumed by React board components.
design\releases\0_1_0\B_99_mobile_status_change_no_update.md:22:This path was added for [[B-87]], and current tests prove remote file refresh but only change card body. They do not prove that remote `status` changes publish granular events or move card between rendered mobile columns. Reported reload requirement therefore remains an unverified regression; current code does not need separate card-status WebSocket message when `watchProject` works.
design\releases\0_1_0\B_99_mobile_status_change_no_update.md:26:- Add integration coverage where a `watchProject` event arrives after mobile project load, remote `loadFile` returns same card with changed `status`, and `DataService` publishes path-scoped `status`, collection `status`, and collection `ordering` events.
design\releases\0_1_0\B_99_mobile_status_change_no_update.md:28:- Run regression against current path first. Fix first boundary that fails: server watch delivery, remote file load, card reconciliation, granular event publication, or leaf subscription. Keep existing `watchProject` protocol unless server does not emit a file event.
design\releases\0_1_0\B_99_mobile_status_change_no_update.md:37:- Desktop project watching and local card moves remain unchanged.
design\architecture\architectural_decisions.md:30:| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |
design\releases\0_1_0\F_130_drop_card_has_too_many_renders.md:21:`CardView.handleDragEnd` calls `cardDragDropService.endDrag()` before `dataService.cards.moveCard()`. Clearing drag state immediately removes drop preview and overlay; card move then rebuilds project snapshot and publishes column membership changes. Destination column can therefore render once without preview or moved card, then again with moved card.
design\releases\0_1_0\F_143_make_parsed_card_the_canonical_in_memory_object.md:52:6. Keep the external-change path: when the watcher reports an out-of-band change to a card file, re-parse that file into a fresh canonical model and replace it, using the existing in-flight echo suppression. Conflict policy for a card with unsaved local changes must match today's behavior.
design\releases\0_1_0\F_143_make_parsed_card_the_canonical_in_memory_object.md:60:- An external (agent) edit arrives for a card that has pending unflushed local changes.
design\releases\0_0_3\F_85_codex_app_server_activity_backend.md:78:- Renderer reload or remote reconnect: recover active execution activity through existing execution replay; recover only current in-memory rate limits.
design\releases\0_1_0\F_142_improve_board_view_on_mobile.md:23:Implementation wise: we should not try to put this all in the same workspace, instead we should have something specific for mobile which only shows 1 column. which column it shows is controlled through a service (standard pattern: service has prop & raises events, menu items set, column updates.
design\releases\0_1_0\F_142_improve_board_view_on_mobile.md:36:- Add service-owned selected mobile column state and change event. Select first visible column by default and when current selection is no longer visible.
design\releases\0_1_0\F_142_improve_board_view_on_mobile.md:37:- Show visible columns in mobile hamburger drawer; selecting one updates service and closes drawer.
design\releases\0_1_0\F_148_simplify_card_state_ownership.md:59:Watcher updates must be parsed and applied deliberately. Ignore the app's own commit echoes as today. If an external update conflicts with a dirty local field, report the conflict and preserve the local change. Do not replace a complete card merely because one external field changed.
design\releases\0_0_5\B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md:18:We should verify if every message type is correctly implemented over websockets
design\releases\0_0_5\B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md:22:Electron's project watcher emits card changes through `watchProject`. Remote-control server forwards them as WebSocket `watchProject` events, and `RemoteControlStorageService` invokes registered callback. `ProjectLoading` then tries to reload changed markdown file, but stops because remote storage does not implement optional `loadFile`. Card therefore stays stale on mobile. Desktop storage implements `loadFile` through same dispatcher.
design\releases\0_0_5\B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md:26:- Add `RemoteControlStorageService.loadFile` and proxy it through existing WebSocket request protocol. Server dispatcher already exposes method.
design\releases\0_0_5\B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md:27:- Keep existing `watchProject` event and project reload flow; no separate card-change message needed.
design\releases\0_0_5\B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md:29:- Audit all server-push message names and payloads against client handlers: `watchProject`, `agentRun`, `actionRun`, `codexRateLimits`, and `worktreesChanged`. Cover subscription setup and cleanup.
design\releases\0_0_5\B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md:34:- Added, changed, and removed markdown files received through `watchProject` update mobile project state.
design\releases\0_0_5\B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md:37:- Existing Electron project watching remains unchanged.
design\feature_descriptions\F_152_open_github_repository_from_electron.md:14:When the react app is connected through a remote connection (websockets), the app is able to open a repository, but only from the user's own account.
design\feature_descriptions\B_91_cardsview_columns_did_not_update_after_auto_change_card_state.md:5:title: cardsview columns did not update after auto change card state
design\feature_descriptions\B_91_cardsview_columns_did_not_update_after_auto_change_card_state.md:14:an agent changed the state of a card to ready, but the UI did not get updated. the card remained in the old column, did not move to the 'ready' column.
design\feature_descriptions\B_91_cardsview_columns_did_not_update_after_auto_change_card_state.md:16:This occured while using websockets
design\releases\0_0_3\F_86_codex_conversation_activity_frontend.md:76:- Remote-control disconnect: retain only current client-memory snapshot, mark stale/hide it, and resubscribe on reconnect.
design\releases\0_0_3\F_86_codex_conversation_activity_frontend.md:84:- Add `CodexRateLimitService` tests for subscription, replacement, staleness, reconnect, and no persistence.
design\feature_descriptions\B_88_save_state_is_not_pushed_to_website.md:28:Before an Electron agent starts or restarts, `runElectronAction` flushes aggregate pending changes. Later agent file writes return through project watcher events. App-generated watcher echoes are suppressed; a real external write against a still-dirty document produces quoted conflict message and preserves local text. That warning is now intentional conflict protection, not evidence that Electron and React maintain independent save states.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_030_remote_bridge_global_spoofing.md:27:- Remote mode still routes action/agent/schedule calls through the WebSocket storage service.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_026_external_files_not_imported.md:3:title: external non-conforming files are not imported as new cards
design\releases\0_0_2\B_026_external_files_not_imported.md:25:- Extend the project watcher path so a newly appearing working-folder `.md` file triggers the same import (debounced, and ignoring writes the app itself just made).
design\releases\0_0_2\B_026_external_files_not_imported.md:26:- Surface imports to the user (e.g. workspace notice: "Imported N external files as new cards") and record a telemetry event.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_040_background_project_load_silent_failure.md:14:`ProjectLoading.loadFullProjectInBackground` (`app/src/services/project_loading.ts`) wraps the whole background phase — full project load, repository file listing, external card import merge — in a catch that only does `console.error`. When it fails (network drop on GitHub, revoked token mid-session, bridge error), the app keeps running on the root-only snapshot: history/architecture cards never load, search over special folders silently returns nothing, `repositoryFiles` stays empty so the affects editor has no suggestions. The user gets no signal that they are working with partial data. This contradicts the B-024 policy that errors surface through the workspace notice + telemetry path.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_044_typecheck_broken_missing_import.md:3:title: typecheck broken on main - missing MarkdownFile import in external card import tests
design\releases\0_0_2\B_044_typecheck_broken_missing_import.md:17:src/services/external_card_import_service.test.ts(8,28): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'MarkdownFile'.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_044_typecheck_broken_missing_import.md:20:The J-014 test split (commit 97feeb4) annotated the fixture array in `app/src/services/external_card_import_service.test.ts` with `MarkdownFile[]` without importing the type from `../data/data_types`. Tests still pass because vitest does not typecheck, so the break is invisible until someone runs `npm run typecheck` — which means the policy gate the repo relies on is currently red for every branch cut from main.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_044_typecheck_broken_missing_import.md:27:- The external card import tests still pass.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_047_remote_control_connection_errors.md:14:Every remote-control connection failure in `app/src/services/remote_control_storage_service.ts` surfaces as the same `'Remote-control connection failed'` error: unreachable server, refused socket, invalid token (server responds 401 on upgrade), and occupied server all look identical to the user. In addition, `ensureConnected` has no timeout — a server that accepts TCP but never completes the WebSocket handshake leaves the promise pending and the UI stuck in its loading state indefinitely. Finally, `loadRemoteBranches` in `app/src/components/shell/project/use_project_toolbar_menu_actions.ts` swallows the branch-list failure in its catch block; verify the session service's error state actually reaches the user in the open-project dialog.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_046_remote_control_single_connection.md:14:The remote-control WebSocket server (`desktop/src/integrations/remote_control_service.js`) accepts any number of authenticated clients: the `connection` handler just adds the client to the set and increments `clientCount`, and the toolbar label ("Remote N") even anticipates multiples. The intended policy for now is **max one connection**; any further connection attempt must be refused. There is also no way for a refused client to learn *why* it was refused, so the web app cannot show a meaningful "server is occupied" message — every failure surfaces as the generic browser socket error.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_046_remote_control_single_connection.md:17:- Server: when a client is already connected, refuse the next connection. Do it in a way the browser WebSocket API can observe: complete the upgrade, then immediately close with a dedicated close code and reason (e.g. `4409` / `"occupied"`). Browsers hide HTTP upgrade responses, so refusing at the HTTP level (409) would be indistinguishable from a network error on the client.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_046_remote_control_single_connection.md:26:- Tests cover: second-connection refusal, occupied error mapping in the client service, and reconnect-after-disconnect.
design\releases\0_0_2\B_066_running_actions_contract_gaps_after_f047.md:145:Fix direction: no code change required by the contract. Record it as an accepted limitation in `running_actions.md` ("Application-level triggers") — note: modifying that architecture document needs explicit approval first. If instead triggers should move to Electron, that is a separate feature (Electron would need card-state diffing on `watchProject` events).
design\releases\0_0_2\F_008_templates_and_headers.md:23:- Keep headers optional for imported/external files; files without naming convention remain imported as new feature cards.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_013_desktop_app.md:19:Remote control is not implemented yet: there is no WebSocket server or toolbar flow to start/stop it. Agent execution is also not implemented yet: there is no process runner, stdin/stdout/stderr capture, log persistence or card-to-log linking.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_013_desktop_app.md:25:- Add a remote-control command in the React toolbar that asks Electron to start/stop a WebSocket server and reports connection state back to the UI.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_013_desktop_app.md:30:- Surface failures from folder selection, Git commands, file watching, WebSocket startup and agent execution as user-visible errors.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_013_desktop_app.md:36:- The app can start and stop remote-control mode from the UI, and Electron exposes a WebSocket endpoint only while remote control is active.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_005_card_view.md:23:- Ordering: derive column order from `after`, where `after` stores the preceding card's `internalId`. Dragging within a column updates `after`; dragging between columns updates `status` and `after`. Use `@dnd-kit` (`@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/sortable`, with `@dnd-kit/modifiers` as needed) for drag-and-drop — chosen for built-in touch/pointer support (desktop + mobile), a sortable model that fits cross-column moves, and its lightweight, TypeScript-native, accessible API. On drop, persist only the two/three cards whose `after` values changed.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_026_external_change_watching.md:14:Reflect external markdown file additions, removals and changes in the app while a local project is open (F-002 acceptance criterion), including importing newly discovered files that don't follow the naming convention as new feature cards.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_026_external_change_watching.md:17:`local_git_service.js` `watchProject` already emits events for `.md` and `.json` changes under the project root, but `DataService.handleProjectWatchEvent` (`app/src/services/data_service.ts`) only reacts to action-definition JSON paths and silently drops every markdown event. Externally created/edited/deleted markdown files therefore never appear (or disappear) until the project is reopened, and the "import as new feature during usage" behavior from `data management.md` never triggers at runtime.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_026_external_change_watching.md:29:- Editing a file externally updates the card/tab content when it has no unsaved in-app edits.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_026_external_change_watching.md:30:- Deleting a file externally removes its card and closes its tab.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:3:title: remote control WebSocket data bridge
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:14:Make "remote control" a real second bridge type, per the architecture: when activated, the Electron app starts a WebSocket server that a remote (browser-hosted) React app can connect to and use as its data service — the same operations the preload bridge offers (project load, commit, actions, agents), transported over WebSocket.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:17:Stub only. `desktop/remote_control_service.js` is a hand-rolled WebSocket **echo server**: it accepts connections and reflects text frames back (`socket.on('data', …)` writes the decoded frame straight back). Frames are capped at 125 bytes, there is no ping/pong, no fragmentation and no message protocol. The React side (`app/src/data/electron_remote_control_bridge.ts`, `app/src/components/shell/remote_control_button.tsx`) only exposes start/stop/status of the server. No data operation crosses the WebSocket, and the React app has no WebSocket-backed `StorageService` implementation, so a remote React app cannot control anything.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:21:- Define a small JSON-RPC-style message protocol: `{ id, method, params }` requests and `{ id, result | error }` responses, plus server-push events (`watchProject` changes, agent run events) as `{ event, payload }` messages.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:23:- On the React side, add a `RemoteControlStorageService` implementing `StorageService` (and the action/agent bridge interfaces) over a WebSocket connection, selected when the app is not running inside Electron and the user enters a remote endpoint.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:32:- Server push delivers `watchProject` and agent run events to connected clients.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_041_remote_connect_button_and_dialog.md:17:There is no Connect button in the browser: `app/src/components/shell/remote_control_button.tsx` renders `null` when the Electron bridge is absent. The only way to reach a remote server is the "Remote" source inside the open-project dialog (`app/src/components/shell/project/project_open_dialog.tsx`), whose endpoint/token fields always start empty even though the last-used values are persisted in localStorage by `app/src/data/remote_control_connection.ts` (they are read on reconnect, just never fed back into the form).
design\releases\0_0_2\F_045_electron_serves_web_app_http.md:17:The remote-control HTTP server in `desktop/src/integrations/remote_control_service.js` also serves the bundled React build (the same `app/dist` already packaged with Electron) on GET requests; WebSocket upgrade handling stays as is. One server, one port.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_045_electron_serves_web_app_http.md:19:Why plain http works here: the page origin is `http://…`, which is not a secure context, so browsers allow plain `ws://` from it — the mixed-content blocking that forces `wss://` only applies to https-delivered pages. Page and socket are same-origin (same host, same port), so there is no CORS and no endpoint entry: the web app derives the WebSocket URL from `window.location`.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_045_electron_serves_web_app_http.md:30:- Static serving and WebSocket upgrade coexist on one port; unauthorized WebSocket connects are still refused; max-1 policy (B-046) unaffected.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_053_card_number_from_header_id.md:29:- Both call sites (`createCardFile` in `card_naming.ts` and `planExternalCardImports` in `app/src/services/external_card_import_service.ts`) already receive `MarkdownFile[]` with content loaded, so no signature change or extra reads are needed.
design\releases\0_0_2\J_006_split_local_git_service.md:20:- `desktop/project_files.js` — load project/root/config, read/write/delete/move files, working-folder template, watchProject.
design\releases\0_0_2\J_001_initialize.md:28:  - Scaffold a minimal Electron main process that opens a `BrowserWindow` and loads that URL. A `preload.js` stub is created as the future bridge (file-system access, agents, WebSocket "remote control") but no bridge logic is implemented in this job.

design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:14:Make "remote control" a real second bridge type, per the architecture: when activated, the Electron app starts a WebSocket server that a remote (browser-hosted) React app can connect to and use as its data service — the same operations the preload bridge offers (project load, commit, actions, agents), transported over WebSocket.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:17:Stub only. `desktop/remote_control_service.js` is a hand-rolled WebSocket **echo server**: it accepts connections and reflects text frames back (`socket.on('data', …)` writes the decoded frame straight back). Frames are capped at 125 bytes, there is no ping/pong, no fragmentation and no message protocol. The React side (`app/src/data/electron_remote_control_bridge.ts`, `app/src/components/shell/remote_control_button.tsx`) only exposes start/stop/status of the server. No data operation crosses the WebSocket, and the React app has no WebSocket-backed `StorageService` implementation, so a remote React app cannot control anything.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:21:- Define a small JSON-RPC-style message protocol: `{ id, method, params }` requests and `{ id, result | error }` responses, plus server-push events (`watchProject` changes, agent run events) as `{ event, payload }` messages.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:23:- On the React side, add a `RemoteControlStorageService` implementing `StorageService` (and the action/agent bridge interfaces) over a WebSocket connection, selected when the app is not running inside Electron and the user enters a remote endpoint.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_032_remote_control_bridge.md:32:- Server push delivers `watchProject` and agent run events to connected clients.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_041_remote_connect_button_and_dialog.md:17:There is no Connect button in the browser: `app/src/components/shell/remote_control_button.tsx` renders `null` when the Electron bridge is absent. design\releases\0_0_2\F_045_electron_serves_web_app_http.md:17:The remote-control HTTP server in `desktop/src/integrations/remote_control_service.js` also serves the bundled React build (the same `app/dist` already packaged with Electron) on GET requests; WebSocket upgrade handling stays as is. One server, one port.
design\releases\0_0_2\F_045_electron_serves_web_app_http.md:19:Why plain http works here: the page origin is `http://…`, which is not a secure context, so browsers allow plain `ws://` from it — the mixed-content blocking that forces `wss://` only applies to https-delivered pages. Page and socket are same-origin (same host, same port), so there is no CORS and no endpoint entry: the web app derives the WebSocket URL from `window.location`.

When connected through a websocket, when the backend changes the state of a card, the react side is not notified. A reload is currently needed. Most likely a missing message

## Current state

Here, card state means `status` in card Markdown frontmatter. Electron's project watcher sends file changes as `watchProject` WebSocket events. Mobile client then requests changed file through `RemoteControlStorageService.loadFile`; `ProjectLoading` reparses it, and `DataService` should publish card-level and collection-level `status` events consumed by React board components.

This path was added for [[B-87]], and current tests prove remote file refresh but only change card body. They do not prove that remote `status` changes publish granular events or move card between rendered mobile columns. Reported reload requirement therefore remains an unverified regression; current code does not need separate card-status WebSocket message when `watchProject` works.

## implementation details

- Add integration coverage where a `watchProject` event arrives after mobile project load, remote `loadFile` returns same card with changed `status`, and `DataService` publishes path-scoped `status`, collection `status`, and collection `ordering` events.
- Add mobile React coverage proving changed card leaves old column and appears in new column without reopening project or remounting board.
- Run regression against current path first. Fix first boundary that fails: server watch delivery, remote file load, card reconciliation, granular event publication, or leaf subscription. Keep existing `watchProject` protocol unless server does not emit a file event.
- Preserve watcher debounce, dirty-document conflict protection, subscription cleanup, and Electron behavior.

## acceptance criteria

- After Electron-side process changes loaded card's frontmatter `status`, connected mobile board shows card in destination column after normal watcher debounce, without manual reload.
- Old column no longer contains card, and any open status control shows new value.
- Remote status update publishes only required card and collection events; unrelated card fields do not rerender.
- Added, changed, and removed remote Markdown handling from [[B-87]] still works.
- Desktop project watching and local card moves remain unchanged.

When an agent changes a card and the app is running in electron, the app gets updates and the card refreshed. This does not happen when app is on mobile and connected to electron.

We should verify if every message type is correctly implemented over websockets

## Current state

Electron's project watcher emits card changes through `watchProject`. Remote-control server forwards them as WebSocket `watchProject` events, and `RemoteControlStorageService` invokes registered callback. `ProjectLoading` then tries to reload changed markdown file, but stops because remote storage does not implement optional `loadFile`. Card therefore stays stale on mobile. Desktop storage implements `loadFile` through same dispatcher.

## implementation details

- Add `RemoteControlStorageService.loadFile` and proxy it through existing WebSocket request protocol. Server dispatcher already exposes method.
- Keep existing `watchProject` event and project reload flow; no separate card-change message needed.
- Add regression coverage for watch event followed by remote file load and refreshed project state.
- Audit all server-push message names and payloads against client handlers: `watchProject`, `agentRun`, `actionRun`, `codexRateLimits`, and `worktreesChanged`. Cover subscription setup and cleanup.

## acceptance criteria

- Agent change to card file appears on connected mobile app without reopening project.
- Added, changed, and removed markdown files received through `watchProject` update mobile project state.
- Remote `loadFile` returns same markdown payload and errors as Electron bridge.
- Every server-push message type has matching client handling and round-trip test coverage.
- Existing Electron project watching remains unchanged.

The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - After history is selected, `handleConversationChange` only loads persisted paths, so popup cannot return to empty conversation state.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep empty `Conversations` item selectable while picker is enabled.\\r\\n- Treat empty value as reset: clear selected conversation and displayed chat without calling conversation loader.\\r\\n- Next run omits `continueFrom` and starts new conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- User can select `Conversations` after selecting historical conversation.\\r\\n- Popup returns to empty conversation without error or empty-path load.\\r\\n- Next run starts new conversation; selecting history still continues selected conversation.\\r\\n- Picker and controller tests cover reset and continuation behavior.\\r\\n\\n===== F_115_add_support_for_request_approval.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_115\\r\\ninternalId: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\r\\ntitle: add support for request approval\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\n---\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`CodexStreamingAdapter` handles structured questions, but not Codex app-server approval requests. `item/fileChange/requestApproval` and `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` fall through as protocol diagnostics, for example `item/fileChange/requestApproval: unknown (...)`. No approval UI or JSON-RPC response exists, so the turn remains blocked.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Handle both approval methods as server-initiated JSON-RPC requests before notification handling. Validate request, item, thread, and turn ids; track pending requests by request id; clear them on `serverRequest/resolved`.\\r\\n- Add a dedicated approval contract through `AgentRunnerService`, action execution events, Electron preload/local bridge, and remote control. Respond with `{ decision }`; for command requests, honor `availableDecisions` when supplied. Keep approvals separate from structured questions and conversation messages.\\r\\n- Store pending approvals in `ActionExecutionService`. Keep execution `waitingForInput` while any question or approval remains. Replay must restore unresolved approvals and discard resolved ones after renderer reload.\\r\\n- Add a separate popup approval component. Show reason plus command, working directory, parsed actions, network host/protocol, requested permissions, or affected file paths when available. Actions sit bottom-right: allow once, allow for session, decline, and stop turn. Show policy-amendment choices only when Codex supplies them.\\r\\n- Support multiple pending approvals without overwriting one another. Disable a submitted request until response or resolution; reject duplicate, stale, mismatched, or unsupported decisions clearly.\\r\\n- Do not persist approval requests or decisions in conversation/activity files or agent handoff context. Existing completed command/file activity remains authoritative.\\r\\n- Add adapter, runner, execution-contract, bridge, remote-control, service, popup, reload, and regression tests. Run lint and tests in `desktop/` and `app/`.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- File-change and command-execution approval requests show actionable prompts instead of protocol diagnostics.\\r\\n- Allow once/session, decline, stop-turn, and offered policy-amendment choices send the exact matching JSON-RPC decision and unblock Codex.\\r\\n- Approval UI shows available security context before user decides, including network-specific context when present.\\r\\n- Concurrent requests remain isolated; `serverRequest/resolved`, turn completion, or cancellation removes only matching pending requests.\\r\\n- Renderer reload and remote-control clients retain correct pending approval state.\\r\\n- Structured questions, activity ordering, changed-path tracking, and conversation persistence keep existing behavior; approval data is not persisted.\\r\\n\\n===== F_89_add_support_for_clicking_on_links_in_chatlogs.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_89\\r\\ninternalId: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\ntitle: add support for clicking on links in chatlogs\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: e69b9faf-30dd-4ad6-9d99-7e6af4d18c76\\r\\n---\\r\\nSometimes the agent produces a link to a local project file. Currently, when the user clicks on this link, the system crashes.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhat should happen: if it is a md file or action-json file in the design folder (or subfolder), show it in the list view with the correct editor. Otherwise, open it with vscode (externally)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionConversationChat` renders messages with `ReactMarkdown` without a custom link handler. Local paths therefore use browser navigation and can crash the Electron renderer.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe app already opens loaded Markdown and action-definition JSON files through `workspaceNavigationService` and `openFilesService`. VS Code opening exists through the Electron `openInEditor` bridge, but is currently used only for diff lines.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Intercept local-file links in `ActionConversationChat`; prevent browser navigation and report failures through `dialogService`.\\r\\n- Accept repository-relative paths and absolute Windows paths. Normalize separators and convert paths inside the active repository to repository-relative paths.\\r\\n- When the target is inside configured `projectFolder` and is either a Markdown file or a loaded action-definition JSON file, switch to list view and open its existing Markdown or action editor.\\r\\n- Open every other local project file in VS Code through the Electron bridge. Keep normal web-link behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Reject paths outside the active repository and missing targets without crashing.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Clicking relative or absolute Windows links to Markdown files under configured `projectFolder` opens them in list view with the Markdown editor.\\r\\n- Clicking relative or absolute Windows links to action-definition JSON files under configured `projectFolder` opens them in list view with the action editor.\\r\\n- Clicking another local project-file link opens that file in VS Code.\\r\\n- Invalid, missing, or out-of-project file links show an error and leave app usable.\\r\\n- Tests cover path normalization, internal editor routing, VS Code fallback, and error handling.\\r\\n\\n===== F_90_redesign_add_new_card_dialog.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_90\\r\\ninternalId: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\\r\\ntitle: redesign add new card dialog\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d97a054f-5a67-47bb-9070-df874cf9148e\\r\\n---\\r\\nReference mockup: `New Card Dialog.dc.html` (desktop + mobile side by side, light/dark toggle top-right).\\r\\nStyle tokens and component conventions: `STYLE_GUIDE.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Why\\r\\n\\r\\nThe current dialog is low-value and hard to scan:\\r\\n\\r\\n* The markdown template (Goal / Current status / Details / Tasks) is pre-inserted and rendered as large bold headings, so it dominates the dialog, doesn't look editable, and must be deleted for most cards.\\r\\n* Title â€” the one field that always matters â€” is visually secondary.\\r\\n* Type is a dropdown, which costs two clicks for a short, known list.\\r\\n* The footer's \\\"Adds to \\\\<column>\\\" is static text, so the target column can't be changed without closing the dialog.\\r\\n* Net result: lots of empty space, little usefulness.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Scope\\r\\n\\r\\nTwo presentations of the same form and the same state:\\r\\n\\r\\n* **Desktop** â€” centered modal dialog over a scrim.\\r\\n* **Mobile** â€” full-height sheet.\\r\\n\\r\\nSame fields, same validation, same submit behavior. Only layout, control sizing, and chrome differ. Breakpoint should follow whatever the app already uses; do not introduce a new one.\\r\\n\\r\\n***\\r\\n\\r\\n## Field order and behavior (both platforms)\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1. Title â€” primary field\\r\\n\\r\\n* First element in the body, autofocused on open.\\r\\n* Visually the largest input: \\\\~17px/600 on desktop, \\\\~18px/600 on mobile.\\r\\n* Placeholder `Card titleâ€¦`.\\r\\n* Required. Create is disabled (or shows an inline error) while empty. Trim before submit.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2. Type â€” single-select pill row\\r\\n\\r\\n* Replaces the dropdown with one-click pills.\\r\\n* **Types are dynamic.** Render one pill per type from the app's existing type source (same source the board/card already uses). Do not hard-code type names, count, or order â€” the row must work for 2 types or 12.\\r\\n* **Colors are dynamic.** Each pill shows a small round dot (8px) filled with that type's own color, taken from the type record. Never hard-code hex values per type; if a type has no color, fall back to a neutral token (`--text-4`).\\r\\n* Selected state: tinted background + border in the app's primary token, primary text color. Unselected: subtle track background, secondary text, transparent border; hover raises contrast.\\r\\n* Default selection: the app's existing default type (first in the list if there is no configured default).\\r\\n* Overflow: desktop wraps to multiple lines; mobile scrolls horizontally in one row (no wrap, no visible scrollbar chrome).\\r\\n* Keyboard: arrow keys move between pills, Space/Enter selects; the row is a single tab stop (radiogroup semantics â€” `role=\\\"radiogroup\\\"` with `role=\\\"radio\\\"` + `aria-checked` children).\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== F_91_remove_finished_reasoning_blocks.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_91\\r\\ninternalId: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\ntitle: remove finished reasoning blocks\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen a reasoning output of an agent finishes, we should remove the block\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\nCodex reasoning is stored as an `AgentConversationEvent`. Streaming updates replace the same event by `providerItemId`, changing its status from `inProgress` to `completed`. `ActionConversationChat` currently renders every reasoning event, so completed reasoning blocks remain visible during the live run and in reopened conversations. Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\r\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\r\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\r\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\r\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\r\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\r\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\r\\n\\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_94\\r\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\r\\n\\r\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\\r\\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\\r\\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\\r\\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\r\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\r\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\r\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\r\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\r\\n\\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_95\\r\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\r\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard commit history reads tracked `<projectFolder>/activity/card__<cardInternalId>.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\r\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\\r\\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Do not model it as a user action.\\r\\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\\r\\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\\r\\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\\r\\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\r\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\r\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\r\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\r\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\r\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\r\\n\\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_96\\r\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\\r\\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\\r\\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\\r\\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\\r\\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\\r\\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\\r\\n\\n===== F_98_worktree_vs_project_folder_placeholders.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_98\\r\\ninternalId: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\ntitle: worktree vs project folder placeholders\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\n---\\r\\nWe have 'rootProjectFolder' placeholder. this currently maps to the folder that the agent is running on, so it could the the main project folder or a worktree. \\r\\n\\r\\nWe need to improve this and split it up in `worktree-folder` and 'project-folder' where the last one always references the main project folder while 'worktree-folder' references the folder that the agent is currently running in.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso, we need to add the 'releases-folder' as well\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` exists in action prompt/command and diff-command placeholder sets.\\r\\n- Action execution resolves it to the execution checkout, which may be the opened project folder or a linked worktree. Diff commands resolve it to the opened project folder.\\r\\n- Action editor insertion controls and user documentation expose only the existing placeholder.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Replace `{{rootProjectFolder}}` everywhere with `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}`; do not keep a legacy alias.\\r\\n- `{{worktree-folder}}` resolves to the absolute execution checkout path. When no linked worktree is selected, it equals `{{project-folder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{project-folder}}` always resolves to the absolute opened repository path, including during linked-worktree execution.\\r\\n- Add `{{releases-folder}}`, resolving to the configured repository-relative releases path: `<projectFolder>/<releasesFolder>`.\\r\\n- Support all three placeholders in action prompts, action commands, prompt preparation, diff commands, editor insertion controls, validation, and documentation.\\r\\n- Fail before process start when a required placeholder value is unavailable. Add tests for primary and linked-worktree execution, custom release paths, diff commands, insertion controls, and removed `{{rootProjectFolder}}` support.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Primary-checkout actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- Linked-worktree actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` to that worktree and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- `{{releases-folder}}` returns the configured path relative to repository root, independent of active checkout.\\r\\n- Action prompts, action commands, and diff commands use the same three folder placeholders.\\r\\n- Editors and documentation list the new placeholders and no longer list `{{rootProjectFolder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` is not resolved.\\r\\n\\n===== J_020_unify_agent_conversation_entries.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-020\\r\\ninternalId: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\ntitle: unify agent conversation messages and events into ordered entries\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - shared/agent_conversations.mjs\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_conversation.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_transcript.js\\r\\n  - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/agents/card_agent_state.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the parallel agent-conversation `messages` and `events` arrays with one canonical ordered `entries` array. Array position is ingestion order and is the only display order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis refactor must land before the action-popup rendering-isolation work. That work must consume the single entry list and must not preserve the current merge-and-sort path.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Conversation entry**: one ordered item in an agent conversation.\\r\\n- **Message entry**: user or assistant text.\\r\\n- **Event entry**: reasoning, tool use, command execution, diagnostics, failures, and lifecycle observations.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not use **activity** for a conversation entry, field, helper, component, or collection. `activity` remains valid only for the separate card/project activity-storage domain.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPersisted `AgentConversation` stores `messages` and `events` separately. Live execution repeats the split as `LiveAgentTurn.messages` and `LiveAgentTurn.activities`. Producers append or replace items in those separate collections, while chat and transcript consumers merge and sort them by `sequence` to reconstruct ingestion order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe split causes:\\r\\n\\r\\n- duplicate persisted and live representations;\\r\\n- inconsistent `event`/`activity` terminology;\\r\\n- repeated merge and sort work in consumers;\\r\\n- a rebuilt full `AgentConversation` projection in the popup controller;\\r\\n- ordering behavior owned by presentation code instead of the producer.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required model\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a discriminated union and one collection:\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts\\r\\n\\n===== J_021_derive_markdown_styles_globally.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-021\\r\\ninternalId: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\ntitle: derive active Markdown content styles once in the global theme\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/theme_context.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/theme_provider.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/theme_provider.test.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/use_app_theme.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/editor/markdown_style_sx.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/config/markdown_style_preview.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild the active Markdown content styling once when the global Markdown style configuration changes. Components that render active Markdown consume the stable derived style and never rebuild it during unrelated renders.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job is independent of the action-popup subscription refactor and should land before performance verification of that refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\n`AppThemeProvider` owns `markdownStyleConfig`, but consumers receive only the raw configuration. Both `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` call `buildMarkdownContentSx(markdownStyleConfig)` in their render bodies. The builder creates a new nested MUI style object even when the configuration is unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n`MarkdownStylePreview` also calls the builder, but it renders an explicit configuration draft rather than the active global style.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Derive a stable `markdownContentSx` value in `AppThemeProvider` with `useMemo`, depending only on `markdownStyleConfig`.\\r\\n- Expose the derived value through `AppThemeContextValue` and its fallback value.\\r\\n- Make `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` consume `markdownContentSx` directly.\\r\\n- Do not call `buildMarkdownContentSx` from either component.\\r\\n- Keep `buildMarkdownContentSx` as a pure derivation function owned by the theme/style layer.\\r\\n- Memoize `MarkdownStylePreview`'s derived style by its explicit `config` prop. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - After history is selected, `handleConversationChange` only loads persisted paths, so popup cannot return to empty conversation state.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep empty `Conversations` item selectable while picker is enabled.\\r\\n- Treat empty value as reset: clear selected conversation and displayed chat without calling conversation loader.\\r\\n- Next run omits `continueFrom` and starts new conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- User can select `Conversations` after selecting historical conversation.\\r\\n- Popup returns to empty conversation without error or empty-path load.\\r\\n- Next run starts new conversation; selecting history still continues selected conversation.\\r\\n- Picker and controller tests cover reset and continuation behavior.\\r\\n\\n===== F_115_add_support_for_request_approval.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_115\\r\\ninternalId: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\r\\ntitle: add support for request approval\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\n---\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`CodexStreamingAdapter` handles structured questions, but not Codex app-server approval requests. `item/fileChange/requestApproval` and `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` fall through as protocol diagnostics, for example `item/fileChange/requestApproval: unknown (...)`.
